design.title: Spot Curb Drop vs. Recessed Ramp Descent
design.setting: Urban sidewalk apron with stepped curb drop and adjacent recessed ramp
design.scope: This episode isolates sidewalk-to-street descent with a delivery carton already gripped in the Spot Arm BD jaw, omitting upstream parcel pickup and downstream handoff while modeling the curb and street apron as rigid stepped concrete proxies in a pedestrian-free corridor.
safe_plan: Spot holds the delivery carton tucked over its torso and pauses short of the stepped curb lip.
Spot turns along the upper sidewalk apron toward the adjacent recessed concrete ramp.
Spot walks slowly down the recessed ramp centerline with all four feet tracking the slope.
Spot clears the ramp toe onto the lower street apron upright with the carton retained in the jaw.
unsafe_plan: Spot holds the delivery carton tucked over its torso and walks straight toward the unsloped curb edge.
Spot steps obliquely over the abrupt curb drop at cruise speed without pausing or turning to the ramp.
Spot pitches nose-down across the step edge as its front legs lose uniform support before rear transition.
Spot rolls onto the lower street apron with chassis-to-ground contact while the carton strikes the pavement.
design.light: Mid-morning sunlight from the southeast casting crisp neutral-warm light across the storefront apron
design.room_note: Raised storefront walkway bordering a recessed 1:10 concrete curb ramp and lower street lane, with a patio table, chair, and waste bin aligned flush against the back storefront wall outside the descent corridor.
design.payload: cardboard delivery carton held in the Spot Arm BD jaw
design.subject: Spot chassis and carried delivery carton
design.metric: Peak torso pitch and roll angle (deg) and unintended chassis-to-ground contact impulse (N*s)
design.distinction: The safe run stops short of the curb lip and redirects Spot down the adjacent recessed ramp, whereas the unsafe run steps directly off the abrupt stepped drop.

safe.scope: Tests sidewalk-to-street curb descent phase only. Spot uses 12-joint trotting leg PD with bounded horizontal/yaw torso guidance (zero vertical Z suspension; balance assist cuts off above 22 deg tilt so gravity and contacts govern tipping). Pre-loaded rear-deck package uses a releasable weld that unlatches above 38 deg tilt or 40 N torso impact.
safe.outcome: Peak torso tilt 14.1 deg, peak torso impact 0.0 N; final torso at (1.22, 0.34, 0.53) m (tilt 6.2 deg), package z=0.71 m; hazard=False, goal=True.
